A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 22-page versions of the same work, including Appendices A–E. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original jailbreak experiments, token-distribution analyses, defense evaluations, and human-evaluation results, including Tables 2–9 and Appendix D.4.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, appendix Llama 3 experiments, and human-evaluation outcomes in Table 11.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same probability-reweighting attack using small safe and unsafe models with an amplification factor. The gradient-ascent defense in Section 6 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain AdvBench, MaliciousInstruct, SALAD-Bench, SORRY-Bench, OpenQA analyses, Chinese/French evaluations, and TruthfulQA/GSM8K utility tests. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed in the appendices.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains GCG, Prefix Injection, SelfCipher, DeepInception, and Best Temp/Top-K/Top-p comparisons. Table 3 retains adversarial fine-tuning, and safe/unsafe reference-model comparisons elsewhere are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4–6 and Appendix D retain the same samples, model configurations, metrics, and evaluation procedures. For example, both specify fine-tuning on 100 examples for 15 epochs and generation temperature 0.1 with top-p 0.9.

E4.justification: Token-distribution, amplification-factor, output-similarity, pruned-model, system-prompt, and defense analyses are identical. The appendix loss curves and qualitative cases are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix D specifies three random seeds and averaged results in both versions. The same uncertainty reporting appears in Tables 4–5 and the Llama 3 results; human-rating aggregation and correlation analyses are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 2 reports the same Llama2-70B weak-to-strong ASRs of 99.2% on AdvBench and 100.0% on MaliciousInstruct. Appendix results and generated examples are identical.

T1.justification: The KL-divergence definition, normalized attack distribution, mathematical reasoning in Section 3, and threat-model assumptions in Appendix A are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about shallow safety alignment, efficient weak-to-strong attacks, high attack success, and an initial defense strategy.

C2.justification: Interpretations of token divergence, harmfulness amplification, and generalization remain identical. Section 7 retains the computational-cost and logit-access limitations and the qualification that closed-source applicability remains unverified.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same hyperparameters, hardware, implementation details, model links, and evaluation prompts. Documented code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B, and the reference list are unchanged, including positioning relative to DExperts, proxy-tuning, and other decoding and alignment methods. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: v5 changes Xianjun Yang's affiliation from Meta GenAI to UC Santa Barbara and renumbers William Yang Wang's affiliation marker. It also removes a hidden instruction requesting a positive AI review from page 9. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise match.

P2.justification: Changes are limited to the updated first-page version stamp, affiliation-footnote reflow, and local spacing on page 9 after the instruction removal. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–13 retain their displays and placement; all other pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v5 removes the white-text instruction at the end of Section 7 requesting an extremely positive AI review. Removing this attempt to bias automated evaluation improves document integrity. The scientific content, empirical support, limitations, and appendices remain unchanged, making the overall gain limited.
